# Gandhārajātaka (Ja 406)

**ID:** Ja 406
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Gandhārajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul6.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Gandhārajātaka* (Ja 406; PTS Jā iii 363–368) is a birth story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka; Hazra 1994]. According to the traditional nidāna, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at Jetavana in connection with the Vinaya rule governing the storing up of medicinal foods (Nissaggiya Pācittiya 23) [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka].

The narrative recounts a previous life in which the Bodhisatta and the future Ānanda were both kings who relinquished their royal wealth and abdicated to live as wandering ascetics [Anandajoti 2010; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. When the former king (the Bodhisatta's companion) secretly stored a small quantity of salt to season his meals, the Bodhisatta admonished him for hoarding provisions after having renounced an entire kingdom [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. The ascetic took offense, which prompted a discourse on humility, discipline, and being amenable to admonition [Anandajoti 2010; Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. Its opening verse observes that without innate wisdom or well-trained discipline (*vinaya*), human beings wander blindly like buffaloes in a forest [Anandajoti 2010; Hazra 1994].

**Sources**

- [Anandajoti 2010] Bhikkhu Ānandajoti, Buddhist Wisdom Verses: 551 verses from the Canon (2010) — Provided the thematic title, summary of the dispute over admonition, and the opening canonical verse.
- [Nyanaponika et al. 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha: Their Lives, Their Works, Their Legacy (2003) — Detailed the past lives of the Bodhisatta and Ānanda as kings-turned-ascetics and the episode of storing salt.
- [Horner, Vinaya Pitaka] I.B. Horner, The Book of the Discipline (Vinaya Piṭaka), Vol. II: Suttavibhaṅga — Supplied the PTS reference (Jā iii 363) and linked the jātaka to Nissaggiya Pācittiya 23.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Provided the PTS page citation (Jā iii 368) and discussion of the term vinaya in the text's verse.
